name.text: Calculating the Depth of Water in a Cylindrical Container

questiontext.text:
A spherical container has a diameter of \({@d_sph@}\,\text{cm}. The volume of water is \(\frac{4}{3}\) times the volume of the sphere.

The water is poured into a cylindrical container with a diameter of \({@d_cyl@}\,\text{cm}.\)

Use the volume formula for a sphere to determine the volume of water. Then find the depth of the water in the cylindrical container.

\(\text{The depth of the water}=\)[[input:ans1]]\(\,\text{cm}\)[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

1) Find the radius of the sphere

The diameter of the sphere is \({@d_sph@}\,\text{cm},\) so its radius is

\(r_{\text{sph}}=\frac{{@d_sph@}}{2}\,\text{cm}.\)

2) Calculate the volume of the sphere

The volume of a sphere is \(V=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3.\)

Therefore, the volume of the sphere is

\(V_{\text{sphere}}=\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{{@d_sph@}}{2}\right)^3={@V_sphere@}\,\text{cm}^3.\)

3) Calculate the volume of water

The volume of water is \(\frac{4}{3}\) times the volume of the sphere. Therefore,

\(V_{\text{water}}=\frac{4}{3}V_{\text{sphere}}={@V_water@}\,\text{cm}^3.\)

4) Find the depth of the water in the cylinder

The diameter of the cylinder is \({@d_cyl@}\,\text{cm},\) so its radius is

\(r_{\text{cyl}}=\frac{{@d_cyl@}}{2}\,\text{cm}.\)

The volume of a cylinder is \(V=\pi r^2h.\)

Since the volume of water is unchanged when it is poured into the cylinder,

\(V_{\text{water}}=\pi r_{\text{cyl}}^2h.\)

Hence,

\(h=\frac{V_{\text{water}}}{\pi r_{\text{cyl}}^2}={@h@}\,\text{cm}.\)

Therefore, the depth of the water is

\(\boxed{{@Depth_cylinder@}\,\text{cm}}\).

questionnote.text:
\(\text{The diameter of the sphere}={@d_sph@}\,\text{cm}\)

\(\text{The diameter of the cylinder}={@d_cyl@}\,\text{cm}\)

\(\text{The volume of the sphere}={@V_sphere@}\,\text{cm}^3\)

\(\text{The height of the cylinder}={@depth@}\,\text{cm}\)

You have used \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the volume of the sphere instead of \(\frac{4}{3}\).

The volume of the sphere is

\(V_{\text{sphere}}={@V_sphere@}\,\text{cm}^3.\)

The question states that the volume of water is \(\frac{4}{3}\) times the volume of the sphere. Therefore, the correct volume of water is

\(V_{\text{water}}=\frac{4}{3}V_{\text{sphere}}.\)

You have instead calculated

\(V_{\text{mistake1}}=\frac{3}{4}V_{\text{sphere}}={@V_mistake1@}\,\text{cm}^3.\)

Check how you have interpreted the fraction \(\frac{4}{3}\) in the question, and try again.
